title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0%)
drivers.evidence: No prior price increases in history. Past promotions show average noise-adjusted uplift x1.49. A 6% price rise likely reduces demand, but evidence is limited to one occurrence. Shrink effect toward 1.0 due to uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 13.1. Price increase to $4.08 (+6.0%) is the only known driver. Past promotions show median uplift x2.15 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.49. This price hike is new and not previously tested. The product's ordinary week noise is ±78%, so a 6% price increase is likely to reduce demand. Post-promotion weeks show no lasting lift (x1.08), but no data on price hikes. Given thin evidence and no past price increases, shrink effect toward 1.0. Use conservative downside adjustment.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 13.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 26.3 | 10%-90%: 3.0 - 21.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-78% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
